assignees: INSPUR SUZHOU INTELLIGENT TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.

title: HYBRID SCHEDULING FOR OUT-OF-ORDER PROCESSING
abstract: A processor including reservation stations configured to schedule the execution of instructions of a program is disclosed. The reservations stations may receive instructions from the program based on their type. A first type of reservation station may receive instructions that are processed most efficiently using a dispatch and pick approach that maximizes the capacity of segments in the reservation station. A second type of reservation station receives instructions that are processed most efficiently using a dispatch and pick approach that preserves the program order of the instructions. The reservation stations operate together to provide a hybrid scheduling of the instructions, which can improve processing efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A method for executing a program using a processor, the method comprising: receiving an instruction from the program; decoding the instruction to determine a type of the instruction; determining that the type is sensitive to an order of execution; allocating the instruction to an order-based reservation station of the processor, the order-based reservation station having a plurality of segments; dispatching the instruction to a segment of the plurality of segments according to an order-based dispatch policy of the order-based reservation station; issuing the instruction to an execution unit coupled to the order-based reservation station according to an order-based pick policy of the order-based reservation station; and executing the instruction using the execution unit.

title: CROSS-SITE ROUTING OF INFERENCE WORKLOADS BASED ON PREDICTED POWER AVAILABILITY
abstract: The disclosure presents a technique for routing discrete AI inference workloads to processor clusters co-located with distinct variable-power sources. This technique includes a workload routing process implemented by a cross-site router with four main components: a long-term planner, a short-term planner, a configurator, and a request scheduler. The long-term planner uses workload arrival patterns and long-term predicted power availability at processing sites to generate a first allocation plan for configuring processor frequency and tensor parallelism, and routing inference workloads. The short-term planner uses the first allocation plan and short-term predicted power availability at processing sites to generate a second allocation plan for adjusting processor frequency and routing inference workloads. The configurator allocates processors at the processor clusters based on the first allocation plan and the second allocation plan. The request scheduler routes workload requests to the processing sites based on workload characteristics and the second allocation plan.
first_claim: 1. A method for routing discrete workloads to processor clusters co-located with distinct variable-power sources comprising: generating a first allocation plan based on one or more workload arrival patterns and long-term predicted power availability on a first, longer timescale from one or more distinct variable-power sources; generating a second allocation plan based on the first allocation plan, the one or more workload arrival patterns, and short-term predicted power availability on a second, shorter timescale from the one or more distinct variable-power sources; and allocating the one or more discrete workloads to one or more processor clusters co-located with one of the distinct variable-power sources based on the second allocation plan.

title: Vertical scaling of compute containers
abstract: System, methods, apparatuses, and computer program products are disclosed for auto-scaling of a deployment based on resource utilization data for a workload executing on the deployment. A resource availability is determined based on the resource utilization data and a current resource allocation of the deployment. A severity of resource throttling of the workload may be determined based on the resource utilization data, and a scaling factor is determined based at least on the severity of resource throttling. In response to at least the resource availability satisfying a predetermined condition with a predetermined threshold, the deployment is scaled based on the scaling factor.
first_claim: 1. A method, comprising: determining time-based resource utilization data for a workload executing on a deployment, wherein the resource utilization data comprises one or more of: computational resource utilization data, memory resource utilization data, request latency data, storage resource utilization data, and input/output (I/O) resource utilization data; determining a resource availability based on the resource utilization data and a current resource allocation; determining a severity of resource throttling of the workload based on the resource utilization data; determining a scaling factor based at least on the severity of resource throttling; and automatically scaling, in response to at least the resource availability satisfying a predetermined condition with a predetermined threshold, the deployment based on the scaling factor.

title: FLEXIBLE PARTITIONING OF GPU RESOURCES
abstract: Described herein is a partitionable graphics processor having a plurality of flexibly partitioned processing resources. One embodiment provides a graphics processor comprising a plurality of processing resources configurable to be flexibly partitioned into a plurality of resource partitions and circuitry to compose multiple graphics processor device partitions from the plurality of resource partitions. The multiple graphics processor device partitions are configurable to be asymmetrically composed of different types of functional units.
first_claim: 1-20. (canceled)

title: ENVOY FOR MULTI-TENANT COMPUTE INFRASTRUCTURE
abstract: A data management and storage (DMS) cluster of peer DMS nodes manages data of a tenant of a multi-tenant compute infrastructure. The compute infrastructure includes an envoy connecting the DMS cluster to virtual machines of the tenant executing on the compute infrastructure. The envoy provides the DMS cluster with access to the virtual tenant network and the virtual machines of the tenant connected via the virtual tenant network for DMS services such as data fetch jobs to generate snapshots of the virtual machines. The envoy sends the snapshot from the virtual machine to a peer DMS node via the connection for storage within the DMS cluster. The envoy provides the DMS cluster with secure access to authorized tenants of the compute infrastructure while maintaining data isolation of tenants within the compute infrastructure.
first_claim: 1. A non-transitory computer-readable medium comprising instructions that when executed by one or more processors causes the one or more processors to perform operations comprising: establishing a connection to a data management and storage (DMS) system to provide the DMS system access to one or more virtual machines of a tenant of a multi-tenant cloud compute infrastructure, wherein: the one or more virtual machines are operably connected to a virtual network of the tenant, wherein the virtual network is hosted by the multi-tenant cloud compute infrastructure; the multi-tenant cloud compute infrastructure restricts access by the DMS system to the virtual network of the tenant and to an infrastructure network connecting physical machines including a physical machine that hosts the one or more virtual machines of the tenant; and the infrastructure network and the virtual network use different network layers and share a physical layer; interfacing with the multi-tenant cloud compute infrastructure using a virtualization protocol to generate a snapshot of a first virtual machine of the one or more virtual machines of the tenant; storing the snapshot of the first virtual machine of the tenant in a data store of computing resources provided by the multi-tenant cloud compute infrastructure; and sending the snapshot of the first virtual machine to the DMS system.

title: Capacity cluster resource reservations in a cloud provider network
abstract: Techniques for implementing and utilizing capacity cluster resource reservations are described. A managed compute service receives a user's request to identify a capacity block for use in launching compute instances. A schedule with pre-computed blocks, each corresponding to an amount of instances and an amount of time, is used to identify a block satisfying the request's criteria. The user can later obtain the capacity block and launch instances into the reservation during its time window, where placement rules associated with the reservation ensure the instances are hosted in locations enabling low-latency intercommunications.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: generating, by a managed compute service of a cloud provider network, a schedule including a plurality of blocks of compute capacity hosted by the managed compute service that are available to be reserved by users of the managed compute service, wherein each of the blocks corresponds to compute capacity for a number of compute instances, of a type providing access to graphics processing unit (GPU) processing resources, for a window of time; receiving, at the cloud provider network, a request originated on behalf of a user to find a capacity block, the request identifying a desired number of compute instances and an availability duration for the desired number of compute instances; identifying, by the managed compute service based on use of the schedule, at least a first block of the plurality of blocks as providing compute capacity for the desired number of compute instances for the desired amount of time; transmitting, by the managed compute service, a response to the request that identifies at least the first block, the response including an offering identifier associated with the first block; receiving a request to obtain the first block as a first capacity block for the user, the request including the offering identifier; at a beginning of the window of time corresponding to the first capacity block, updating a data store to change an ownership of the compute capacity for the first block to be associated with an account of the user; and launching one or more compute instances on behalf of the user using the compute capacity.

title: Pipeline techniques for dependent graphics kicks
abstract: Disclosed techniques relate to scheduling sets of graphics work with dependencies. In some embodiments, a first set of graphics work depends on a second set of graphics work. Control circuitry may, in response to a release signal that indicates the second set reaching a first processing point, initiate processing of the first set. Control circuitry may, in response to reaching a kick gate point, stall processing of the first set. Control circuitry may, in response to an end signal for the second set, resume processing of the first set.
first_claim: 1. An apparatus, comprising: graphics processor circuitry; and control circuitry configured to: receive a command stream that indicates different sets of graphics work and schedule sets of graphics work for execution on distributed hardware resources, wherein the command stream includes a first set of work and indicates that the first set of work depends on a second set of work and includes a third set of work and indicates that the third set of work depends on a fourth set of work; in response to an early release signal from the second set of work that indicates that all single-instruction multiple-data (SIMD) groups of the second set of work have been launched, initiate processing of the first set of work by the graphics processor circuitry; stall processing of the first set of work in response to reaching a gate point in the first set of work; resume processing of the first set of work in response to an end signal for the second set of work; and in response to a late release signal from the fourth set of work that indicates that all SIMD groups of the fourth set of work have completed but one or more cleanup operations for the fourth set of work are not complete, initiate processing of the third set of work by the graphics processor circuitry.

title: INTENT IDENTIFICATION AND PREVENTION OF WRONGFUL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RESOURCE PROVISIONING
abstract: Computer-implemented methods for intent identification and prevention of wrongful artificial intelligence (AI) resource provisioning. Aspects include receiving a graphics processing unit (GPU) provision request for a resource to build an AI model. Aspects include generating a provisioner responsibility observer (PRO) score and a training data analyzer (TDA) score. Aspects also include generating an intent score using the PRO score, the TDA score, and domain data associated with the GPU provision request. If the intent score is above a threshold value, aspects include granting access to and monitoring the resource as the AI model is built.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: receiving a graphics processing unit (GPU) provision request for a resource to build an artificial intelligence (AI) model from a user device; generating a provisioner responsibility observer (PRO) score using the GPU provision request; generating a training data analyzer (TDA) score by analyzing training data associated with the GPU provision request; generating an intent score using the PRO score, the TDA score, and domain data associated with the GPU provision request; and in response to determining that the intent score is above a threshold value, granting access to the resource of the GPU provision request and monitoring the resource as the AI model is built.

title: Systems and methods for dynamic provisioning of resources for virtualized
abstract: In one aspect, a method for dynamic provisioning storage for virtual machines by meeting the service level objectives (SLOB) set in the service level agreement (SLA) is provided. The SLA pertains to the operation of a first virtual machine, the method includes the step of monitoring the workload of the first virtual machine. The method includes the step of establishing at least one SLO, typically on performance, in response to the workload. The SLO comprises a set of specific performance targets requirements for a service level of the workload of the first virtual machine that are designed to be met by the provisioned resource so as to comply with the SLA by meeting the SLO. The provisioned resource is associated with the first virtual machine. The method determines an SLA that specifies the first SLO. The SLA comprises a contract that includes consequences of meeting or missing the SLO.
first_claim: 1. A method for dynamic provisioning of storage for virtual machines in a virtualized data center, the method comprising: receiving, at a storage management system, storage requirements for a first virtual machine, wherein the storage requirements are specified by a service level agreement (SLA) for the first virtual machine and include a service level objective (SLO) comprising one or more measurable storage performance targets for storage used by the first virtual machine, and wherein the SLA is a contract that includes consequences of meeting or missing the SLO; assigning, by the storage management system, the first virtual machine to a first logical storage volume located on a first shared data storage based on a determination that the first logical storage volume satisfies the SLO for the first virtual machine; identifying a first input/output flow defined by the first virtual machine and the first logical storage volume; capturing, for the first input/output flow, input/output attributes at an individual input/output packet level to produce a workload fingerprint for the first input/output flow, wherein the input/output attributes include at least one of input/output size, read/write type, sequential or random access pattern, service time, input/output submission rate, or input/output completion rate; monitoring, using the captured input/output attributes, resource usage for the first virtual machine, the first logical storage volume, and the first shared data storage; detecting, based on the monitoring, that the SLO for the first virtual machine is not being met; determining whether the SLO for the first virtual machine is not being met because a second virtual machine, provisioned on a second logical storage volume located on the first shared data storage, is using more performance capacity than specified in a service level agreement associated with the second virtual machine; when the SLO for the first virtual machine is not being met because the second virtual machine is using more performance capacity than specified in the service level agreement associated with the second virtual machine, enforcing the SLA for the first virtual machine by controlling input/output to the first shared data storage, wherein controlling input/output to the first shared data storage comprises at least one of reducing input/output shares allocated to the second virtual machine or limiting an input/output rate allowed into the first shared data storage for the second virtual machine, and wherein enforcing the SLA for the first virtual machine comprises applying, at a storage input/output level, at least one of rate-based input/output traffic shaping or deadline-based scheduling to input/output associated with the first input/output flow; and when the SLO for the first virtual machine is not being met and the second virtual machine is not a cause of the SLO not being met, re-provisioning the first logical storage volume by at least one of modifying the first

title: POLICY-DRIVEN COMPUTING RESOURCE CONSOLIDATION WITH MULTI-LEVEL STATES
abstract: According to an implementation, a hierarchical multi-objective policy enforcement system dynamically manages resources across multiple operational states for computing resource consolidation. The system receives user policies prioritizing performance and operator policies prioritizing efficiency and balances these competing objectives through a policy enforcer that communicates with a global cluster manager coordinating multiple cluster-level managers. Computing resources are consolidated proportionally to collocated consumers, enabling shared standby capacity rather than dedicated resources for each consumer. The system transitions resources between states based on current and predicted workload requirements, with different resource distributions for different utilization scenarios.
first_claim: 1. A system for managing computing resources, comprising: a non-transitory memory storage comprising instructions; and a processor in communication with the non-transitory memory storage, wherein the processor executes the instructions to: identify multiple collocated consumers with reserved computing resources for auto-scaling, monitor actual resource utilization by each of the collocated consumers, consolidate the reserved computing resources proportionally to a number of collocated consumers by sharing standby capacity across the multiple collocated consumers, deactivate a portion of the consolidated reserved computing resources by transitioning them to sleep or shutdown states based on consolidation levels, collect and analyze historical resource usage data to determine usage patterns, trends, or a combination thereof, aggregate trending data of used resources across the collocated consumers, predict reactivation dynamics comprising determining when resources are to be reactivated and in a quantity based on the aggregated trending data, and selectively reactivate inactivated resources from sleep or shutdown states according to the predicted reactivation dynamics before anticipated demand increases.

title: RESOURCE SEARCH METHOD, INFORMATION PROCESSING APPARATUS, AND COMPUTER-READABLE RECORDING MEDIUM
abstract: A non-transitory computer-readable recording medium stores therein a resource search program that causes a computer to execute a process including receiving order information of a logical server from a user using a computer system including composable disaggregated infrastructure, acquiring unused resource information among resources included in a tenant, selecting one or more combinations of resource candidates from the acquired unused resource information based on the order information, based on a straddling number and a weighting for each type of a virtual switch between the resources, calculating a switch straddling estimated number of the virtual switch of a path connecting the resource candidates in the selected combinations to each other, and determining the combination of the resource candidates that minimizes the switch straddling estimated number as resources to be used corresponding to the order information.
first_claim: 1. A non-transitory computer-readable recording medium storing therein a resource search program that causes a computer to execute a process comprising: receiving order information of a logical server from a user using a computer system including composable disaggregated infrastructure; acquiring unused resource information among resources included in a tenant; selecting one or more combinations of resource candidates from the acquired unused resource information based on the order information; based on a straddling number and a weighting for each type of a virtual switch between the resources, calculating a switch straddling estimated number of the virtual switch of a path connecting the resource candidates in the selected combinations to each other; and determining the combination of the resource candidates that minimizes the switch straddling estimated number as resources to be used corresponding to the order information.

title: Device placement optimization with reinforcement learning
abstract: A method for determining a placement for machine learning model operations across multiple hardware devices is described. The method includes receiving data specifying a machine learning model to be placed for distributed processing on multiple hardware devices; generating, from the data, a sequence of operation embeddings, each operation embedding in the sequence characterizing respective operations necessary to perform the processing of the machine learning model; processing the sequence of operation embeddings using a placement recurrent neural network in accordance with first values of a plurality network parameters of the placement recurrent neural network to generate a network output that defines a placement of the operations characterized by the operation embeddings in the sequence across the plurality of devices; and scheduling the machine learning model for processing by the multiple hardware devices by placing the operations on the multiple devices according to the placement defined by the network output.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: receiving data specifying a computational graph that represents a plurality of operations to be placed for distributed processing on a plurality of hardware devices; generating, from the data specifying the computational graph, a sequence of operation embeddings, wherein each operation embedding in the sequence characterizes one or more respective operations of the plurality of operations; processing the sequence of operation embeddings using a placement neural network in accordance with first values of a plurality network parameters of the placement neural network, wherein the placement neural network has an encoder-decoder architecture and is configured to process the sequence of operation embeddings in accordance with the first values to generate a network output defining a placement of the operations characterized by the operation embeddings in the sequence across the plurality of devices; and scheduling the plurality of operations for processing by the plurality of hardware devices by placing the operations on the plurality of devices according to the placement defined by the network output.

title: Image enhancement via iterative refinement based on machine learning models
abstract: A method includes receiving, by a computing device, training data comprising a plurality of pairs of images, wherein each pair comprises an image and at least one corresponding target version of the image. The method also includes training a neural network based on the training data to predict an enhanced version of an input image, wherein the training of the neural network comprises applying a forward Gaussian diffusion process that adds Gaussian noise to the at least one corresponding target version of each of the plurality of pairs of images to enable iterative denoising of the input image, wherein the iterative denoising is based on a reverse Markov chain associated with the forward Gaussian diffusion process. The method additionally includes outputting the trained neural network.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method, comprising: receiving training data from an image database; training, based on the training data, a neural network to predict a high-resolution version of a low-resolution input image, wherein the training comprises denoising score matching to train one or more non-normalized energy functions for density estimation, and wherein the neural network is trained based on a diffusion process comprising: an image corruption process that iteratively adds noise to a high-resolution image, and an image denoising process that learns to reverse the image corruption process by starting from an initial noisy image and iteratively removing noise from the initial image to achieve a target distribution; and providing the trained neural network.

title: Multi-task adapter neural networks
abstract: A system including a multi-task adapter neural network for performing multiple machine learning tasks is described. The adapter neural network is configured to receive a shared input for the machine learning tasks, and process the shared input to generate, for each of the machine learning tasks, a respective predicted output. The adapter neural network includes (i) a shared encoder configured to receive the shared input and to process the shared input to extract shared feature representations for the machine learning tasks, and (ii) multiple task-adapter encoders, each of the task-adapter encoders being associated with a respective machine learning task in the machine learning tasks and configured to: receive the shared input, receive the shared feature representations from the shared encoder, and process the shared input and the shared feature representations to generate the respective predicted output for the respective machine learning task.
first_claim: 1. A system comprising: one or more storage devices; and one or more processors storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to implement a multi-task adapter neural network for performing a plurality of machine learning tasks, wherein the multi-task adapter neural network is configured to: receive a shared input for the plurality of machine learning tasks, and process the shared input to generate, for each of the plurality of machine learning tasks, a respective predicted output; wherein the multi-task adapter neural network comprises: a shared encoder configured to: receive the shared input, and process the shared input to extract shared feature representations for the plurality of machine learning tasks; and a plurality of task-adapter encoders, wherein each of the plurality of task-adapter encoders is associated with a respective machine learning task in the plurality of machine learning tasks and is configured to: receive the shared input, receive the shared feature representations from the shared encoder, and process the shared input and the shared feature representations to generate the respective predicted output for the respective machine learning task, wherein layers of the plurality of task-adapter encoders are arranged in parallel with corresponding layers of the shared encoder, and wherein at least one layer of each task-adapter encoder is configured to receive as input a combination of (i) an output of a layer preceding the corresponding layer of the shared encoder and (ii) an output of a previous layer of the task-adapter encoder.

title: Quantum-Derived Positional Encoding For Large Language Models
abstract: A method and system for training a transformer-based language model, in particular a large language model, or inferring using a transformer-based language model, in particular a large language model, with a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline comprising a classical processor and a quantum processor, wherein . the model comprises a transformer layer, the method comprising: inputting a prompt comprising a sequence of tokens in the classical processor; constructing, with the classical processor, a token graph from the prompt, wherein the token graph comprises a plurality of nodes linked by a plurality of edges, with each token represented by a node in the token graph, and the edges representing semantic, syntactic, and/or statistical relationships between the tokens; evolving the token graph on the quantum processor to generate quantum positional encoding; injecting, by the classical processor, the quantum positional encodings into the model; processing of the prompt by the model using the quantum positional encodings.
first_claim: 1. A method of training a transformer-based language model, in particular a large language model, or inferring using a transformer-based language model, in particular a large language model, with a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline comprising a classical processor and a quantum processor, wherein said model comprises a transformer layer, the method comprising: inputting a prompt comprising a sequence of tokens in the classical processor; constructing, with the classical processor, a token graph from the prompt, wherein the token graph comprises a plurality of nodes linked by a plurality of edges, with each token represented by a node in the token graph, and the edges representing semantic, syntactic, and/or statistical relationships between the tokens; evolving a quantum state associated to the token graph on the quantum processor to generate quantum positional encodings; injecting, by the classical processor, the quantum positional encodings into the model; and processing of the prompt by the model using the quantum positional encodings.

title: GENERATING SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATASETS FROM DIGITAL CONTENT ASSETS UTILIZING A WEIGHTED ROUTER
abstract: The present disclosure relates to systems, non-transitory computer-readable media, and methods for generating a synthetic dataset for machine learning model (“MLM”) training from digital content assets utilizing a weighted router. Specifically, the disclosed systems extract, from digital content assets, content metadata. Additionally, the disclosed systems generate, utilizing a weighted router, MLM prompts comprising a first set of prompts of a first prompt type for one or more MLMs from the content metadata according to a first weight of the weighted router and a second set of prompts of a second prompt type for the one or more MLMs from the content metadata according to a second weight of the weighted router. Further, the disclosed systems generate a synthetic dataset comprising labeled prompts for training the one or more MLMs by generating, utilizing one or more large language models, labels indicating function classifications for the MLM prompts.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: extracting, by at least one processor and from digital content assets, content metadata comprising characteristics of the digital content assets; generating, by the at least one processor utilizing a weighted router, machine learning model prompts comprising: a first set of prompts of a first prompt type for one or more machine learning models from the content metadata according to a first weight of the weighted router; and a second set of prompts of a second prompt type for the one or more machine learning models from the content metadata according to a second weight of the weighted router; and generating a synthetic dataset comprising labeled prompts for training the one or more machine learning models by generating, utilizing one or more large language models, labels indicating function classifications for the machine learning model prompts.

title: KEY VALUE AND EXTENDED TENSOR PARALLELISM FOR TRANSFORMER-BASED NEURAL NETWORKS
abstract: Apparatuses, systems, and techniques to generate inferences for input data. In at least one embodiment, inferences based on input data and using one or more neural networks that include a transformer, with Key-Value (KV) attention heads and partitions of a KV cache of context data of the transformer distributed to different processors. Attention values may be computed for the input data using the distributed KV attention heads and partitions of the KV cache at the different processors. The attention values may be exchanged between the different processors. An output of the transformer may be computed at the different processors using different weight partitions of a Feedforward Network (FFN) of the transformer that are different with respect to the distributed KV attention heads.
first_claim: 1. A processor comprising: a plurality of circuits to generate one or more inferences based on input data and using one or more neural networks comprising a transformer, wherein Key-Value (KV) attention heads and partitions of a KV cache of context data of the transformer are distributed to different ones of the plurality of circuits, and the one or more neural networks are to: compute attention values for the input data using the distributed KV attention heads and partitions of the KV cache at the different ones of the plurality of circuits; exchange the attention values between the plurality of different circuits; and compute an output of the transformer at different ones of the plurality of circuits using different weight partitions of a Feedforward Network (FFN) of the transformer that are different with respect to the distributed KV attention heads.

title: HYBRID DATA PARALLELISM FOR TRANSFORMER-BASED NEURAL NETWORKS
abstract: Apparatuses, systems, and techniques to generate inferences for a batch of input data. In at least one embodiment, inferences for a batch of input data may be generated using one or more neural networks that includes a transformer, where the transformer distributes batch partitions of the batch of input data and Key-Value (KV) attention head partitions that use a KV cache of context data for the inferences to different ones of the processors, computes attention values of the batch partitions with respective to the KV attention head partitions at the different ones of the processors, exchanges two or more of the attention values between the different processors, and computes an output of the transformer at different ones of the processors using different weight partitions of a Feed-forward Network (FFN).
first_claim: 1. A processor comprising: one or more circuits to generate inferences for a batch of input data using one or more neural networks comprising a transformer, wherein the transformer: receives a batch partition of the batch of input data to compute attention values for a Key-Value (KV) attention head partition that uses a KV cache of context data for the inferences, wherein the batch of input data is distributed across a plurality of processors, including the processor, and wherein the KV attention head partition is one of a plurality of KV attention head partitions distributed to the different ones of the plurality of processors; computes attention values of the batch partition with respective to the KV attention head partition at the different ones of the plurality of processors; exchanges two or more of the attention values with other ones of the plurality of different processors; and computes an output based, at least in part, on the exchanged two or more attention values.

title: Reporting for machine learning model updates
abstract: A receiver receives, from a transmitter, a reference neural network. The receiver trains the reference neural network to obtain updated neural network parameters for the reference neural network. The receiver reports to the transmitter in response to a trigger, a difference between the updated neural network parameters and previous neural network parameters for the reference neural network. The trigger may be based on a loss function, a magnitude of the difference between the updated neural network parameters and the previous neural network parameters, and/or a difference between performance of the reference neural network with the updated neural network parameters and performance of the reference neural network with the previous neural network parameters.
first_claim: 1. A method of wireless communication, by a receiver, comprising: receiving, from a transmitter, a reference neural network comprising a trained first portion and an untrained second portion; receiving a request to train only a subset of neural network layers of the reference neural network, the subset of neural network layers comprising the untrained second portion and excludes the trained first portion; training only the subset of the neural network layers of the reference neural network to obtain updated neural network parameters for the subset of the neural network layers of the reference neural network while maintaining the trained first portion unchanged; transmitting a scheduling request in response to a trigger based on at least one of a rate of decrease of a loss function applied during the training falling below a threshold value or a magnitude of a difference between the updated neural network parameters and previous neural network parameters for the subset of the neural network layers of the reference neural network exceeding a threshold; and reporting to the transmitter, using resources allocated in response to the scheduling request, the difference between the updated neural network parameters and the previous neural network parameters for the subset of the neural network layers of the reference neural network.

title: METHOD FOR INTEGRATING TRAINED TRANSFORMER INTO OTHER NEURAL NETWORKS, AND APPARATUS THEREFOR
abstract: The present invention proposes a method for integrating a trained transformer model into other neural networks and operating same without an error, so as to enable harmonious operation with other neural networks by inheriting and expanding training that was already performed without having to retrain a transformer model from the beginning for processing an unknown token that has not been learned.
first_claim: 1. A method performed by a computing device for processing, through a trained neural network comprising n (n is an integer of 1 or greater) stacked encoder or decoder blocks, an unknown token which is not trained by the neural network, the method comprising: inputting an input sequence comprising the unknown token at an i-th token position; and performing a self-attention operation, wherein the performing of the self-attention operation comprises: generating a query matrix, a key matrix, and a value matrix; generating a query-key matrix, based on the query matrix and the key matrix; and for the query-key matrix, replacing one or more matrix elements corresponding to the i-th token position with a predetermined value.

title: Signal source framework for user risk mitigation
abstract: An identity management system may obtain a set of data signals via a system log application programming interface (API). The set of data signals may be associated with interactions between a user of a client device and one or more applications associated with the identity management system. The identity management system may then output a set of text strings that include parsed data from the set of data signals to a large language model (LLM) that is affiliated with a multi-modal machine learning model configured to generate risk metrics based on data signals. A first risk metric may then be obtained from the LLM. Further, the identity management system may generate a second risk metric by using a risk combinator of the multi-modal machine learning model. As such, the identity management system may generate a unified risk metric based on the first risk metric and the second risk metric.
first_claim: 1. A method for risk metric generation, comprising: obtaining, via a system log application programming interface (API) of an identity management system, a plurality of data signals associated with interactions between a user of a client device and one or more applications associated with the identity management system; outputting, to at least one large language model (LLM) affiliated with a multi-modal machine learning model that is configured to generate risk metrics based at least in part on data signals captured via the system log API of the identity management system, a set of text strings comprising parsed data from the plurality of data signals obtained via the system log API; obtaining, from the at least one LLM affiliated with the multi-modal machine learning model, a first risk metric associated with the interactions between the user of the client device and the one or more applications associated with the identity management system; computing a normalized Euclidean Distance between a reference vector and a signal vector corresponding to a subset of the plurality of data signals obtained via the system log API of the identity management system; generating, by a risk combinator of the multi-modal machine learning model, at least one second risk metric associated with the client device, wherein the at least one second risk metric comprises the normalized Euclidean Distance; and generating, by the identity management system, a unified risk metric associated with the user of the client device based at least in part on the first risk metric obtained from the at least one LLM and the at least one second risk metric generated by the risk combinator.

title: Computer-readable recording medium having stored therein machine learning program, method for machine learning, and information processing apparatus
abstract: A method including: obtaining a reduction ratio of each element of layers in a trained model of a neural network; when the neural network includes a process that outputs a tensor as a result of a given calculation on tensors and when tensors from first layers preceding the process are inputted, inserting a second layer that performs a zero padding between the first layers and the process, the first layers including a preceding layer of the process and including one or more layers preceding the preceding layer and being shortcut-connected to the process; and padding tensors inputted into second layers associated one with each first layer with one or more zero matrices such that a number of elements of each tensor inputted into the process from the first layers after reducing of elements of each first layer in accordance with the reduction ratio comes to be a first number.
first_claim: 1. A non-transitory computer-readable recording medium having stored therein a machine learning program, when executed by a processor, for causing a computer to execute a process comprising: obtaining a pruning ratio in a unit of a layer, the pruning ratio representing a reduction ratio of each element of a plurality of layers in a trained model of a neural network including the plurality of layers, the neural network including a calculating process that outputs a tensor serving as a result of a given calculation on a plurality of tensors to be inputted into the calculating process and being inputted with tensors outputted from a plurality of first layers preceding the calculating process into the calculating process, the plurality of first layers being included in the plurality of layers and including the preceding layer of the calculating process and one or more layers preceding the preceding layer, the one or more layers being shortcut-connected to the calculating process; inserting one of a plurality of second layers between each of the plurality of first layers and the calculating process, each of the plurality of second layers performing a zero padding process that pads one or more given elements of the tensors with zero, the plurality of second layers each being associated with each of the plurality of first layers; and padding each of the plurality of second layers with one or more zero matrices such that a number of elements of each of a plurality of tensors inputted into the calculating process from the plurality of first layers of which elements are reduced, the elements being reduced in accordance with the corresponding pruning ratio to each of the first layers, becomes a largest number of elements among the plurality of tensors outputted from the plurality of first layers after the reducing of the elements, re-training a reduced model which is obtained by reducing one or more elements of the plurality of layers in the trained model according to the obtained pruning rate; and determining a pruning rate to be applied to each of the plurality of layers based on inference accuracy of the trained model and inference accuracy of the reduced model having undergone the re-training, the largest number of elements is a number obtained by subtracting a number of elements of a first index common in index representing a position to the plurality of first layers among one or more elements to be reduced in the plurality of first layers from a number of elements when no element is reduced in the plurality of first layers, the padding includes inserting, when an element of a second index representing a position different from a position represented by the first index is not to be reduced in at least one third layer serving as the preceding layer among the plurality of first layers, a zero matrix into the second index of a fourth layer preceding the third layer and serving as one or more layers and being shortcut-connected to the calculating process a

title: Training neural networks through reinforcement learning using standardized absolute deviations
abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including computer programs encoded on a computer storage medium, for training a neural network to perform a machine learning task through reinforcement learning. In one aspect, the training uses importance weights generated using standardized absolute deviations of quality scores generated by the neural network for candidate network outputs.
first_claim: 1. A method for training a neural network that has a plurality of network parameters and that is configured to process a network input in accordance with the network parameters to generate a network output for a machine learning task for the network input, the method comprising: receiving a first training example that comprises a training network input and a target network output for the training network input; processing the training network input using the neural network in accordance with first values of the network parameters to generate (i) a plurality of candidate network outputs for the training network input and (ii) for each candidate network output, a respective first likelihood score for the candidate network output that measures a likelihood that the candidate network output is a correct network output for the training network input as estimated by the neural network in accordance with the first values of the network parameters; for each candidate network output of the plurality of candidate network outputs: generating a respective reward value for the candidate network output based on (i) the candidate network output and (ii) the target network output for the training network input; and generating a respective second training example for the candidate network output that includes (i) the training network input, (ii) the candidate network output, and (iii) the respective reward value for the candidate network output; and computing a respective first importance weight factor for the candidate network output based on the respective first likelihood scores for the plurality of candidate network outputs; obtaining one or more third training examples; obtaining a respective first importance weight factor for each of the third training examples; and training the neural network through reinforcement learning on the third training examples, comprising: for each third training example, determining an importance weight for the third training example based on the respective first importance weight factor for the third training example; for each third training example and in accordance with second values of the network parameters, determining a modified gradient of a reinforcement learning loss using the importance weight and the respective reward value; and updating the second values of the network parameters using the modified gradients for the third training examples.

title: Dynamic Post-Training Compression of Machine Learning Models Using Auto-Tuned Valuation-Based Pruning
abstract: This invention enables post-training compression of machine learning models via auto-tuned valuation-based pruning without retraining. The method, Hallgren Value Pruning (HVP), uses a scoring function of the form V═B·O−k·σ to derive layer-wise pruning thresholds, and was derived from a broader Hallgren Unified Valuation Theory (HUVT) framework. It was validated across large language models (LLMs), convolutional networks (CNNs), multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), and random forests (RFs), achieving up to 59.3% parameter reduction with less than 0.3% accuracy drop, and in some cases, improved perplexity. The framework supports dynamic z-score thresholding and auto-tuned pruning strategies using k, offering a model-agnostic, explainable pruning method.
first_claim: 1. A post-training machine learning model compression method comprising: (a) computing, for each component within a trained model, a valuation score defined by the formula V=B·O−k·σ, where: (i) B represents the standalone utility of the component; (ii) O represents its contextual opportunity or relational contribution; (iii) σ represents statistical uncertainty or variation; and (iv) k is a tunable pruning parameter; (b) ranking said components based on their valuation scores; (c) removing or deactivating components falling below a valuation threshold derived from the pruning parameter k; (d) evaluating the pruned model to ensure performance metrics remain within predefined degradation limits; and (e) wherein the method is performed without need for retraining the model.

title: System and method for natural language processing with pretrained language models
abstract: A computer-implemented system and method and for learning an entity-independent representation are disclosed. The method may include: receiving an input text; identifying named entities in the input text; replacing the named entities in the input text with entity markers; parsing the input text into a plurality of tokens; generating a plurality of token embeddings based on the plurality of tokens; generating a plurality of positional embeddings based on the respective position of each of the plurality of tokens within the input text; generating a plurality of token type embeddings based on the plurality of tokens and the one or more named entities in the input text; and processing the plurality of token embeddings, the plurality of positional embeddings, and the plurality of token type embeddings using a transformer neural network model to generate a hidden state vector for each of the plurality of tokens in the input text.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method for training a computer-implemented language model with entity-independent representation, the method comprising: receiving an input text; identifying one or more proper nouns in the input text; generating entity-marked text based on the input text, wherein generating the entity-marked text includes replacing the identified one or more proper nouns in the input text with one or more entity markers, each of the one or more entity markers corresponding to a respective proper noun in the one or more identified proper nouns; generating a plurality of token embeddings for the input text and the entity-marked text; generating a representation of the input text and a representation of the entity-marked text based on the plurality of token embeddings for the input text and the entity-marked text; inputting the representation of the input text and the representation of the entity-marked text into a computer-implemented language model to train the computer-implemented language model, wherein training the computer-implemented language model includes optimizing a loss function to preserve semantics between the input text and the entity-marked text, wherein the loss function is a function of a semantic error between the input text with the one or more proper nouns and the entity-marked text with the corresponding one or more entity markers, wherein the entity markers and entity-specific token type embeddings are used to learn an entity-independent representation which enables entity swaps and generalization to unseen entities; and storing the trained computer-implemented language model for downstream tasks.

title: ENHANCED TRANSFORMER BASED NEURAL NETWORK ARCHITECTURE WITH ADAPTIVE WEIGHT OPTIMIZATION AND LSTM COMPONENTS
abstract: The present invention discloses a transformer-based neural network architecture including a modified linear transformation layer configured to update weights using a variance-based learning rule during training. The variance-based learning rule is combined with gradient-based updates derived from a loss function to bias weight representations toward higher-variance feature directions. The architecture further includes long short-term memory (LSTM) processing applied within a subset of decoder layers to capture sequential dependencies in input data. The combination of variance-based weight updates and selective LSTM integration provides improved feature representation and sequential processing within transformer-based models.
first_claim: 1. A system for processing sequential data, comprising one or more processors, a memory, and a plurality of programming instructions stored in the memory that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to: process input data using a transformer-based neural network comprising a plurality of decoder layers including self-attention operations and feed-forward neural network operations; replace at least one linear transformation within at least one of the decoder layers with a modified linear transformation layer; during training, update weights of the modified linear transformation layer using a variance-based learning rule based on input activations and corresponding layer outputs, wherein the variance-based learning rule is combined with gradient-based updates derived from a loss function; and a apply long short-term memory (LSTM) processing within a subset of the decoder layers after the self-attention operations and before the feed-forward neural network operations.
